AFTER MEASUREMENT, 2026-08-03, same harnesses and machine as the before note.

Retained footprint of one 4 MiB payload:
  Array[Byte]   8.0 MiB
  Vector[Byte]  19.1 MiB   2.4x the array
  ByteVector     8.2 MiB   1.0x the array
The ~5x memory claim in the bead description was measured at 4.7x before and is now
eliminated: ByteVector retains what the array retains, because it is the array.

Cost of handing 4 MiB to an array, the boundary every codec, digest, ByteBuffer write
and FS2 chunk conversion crosses once per payload:
  Vector[Byte].toArray   2.73 ms    1467 MiB/s
  ByteVector.toArray     0.40 ms    9938 MiB/s
  Array[Byte].clone      0.43 ms    9225 MiB/s
This is the cost the before note identified as the real one, and it is gone: ByteVector
reaches Array.clone parity, a 6.8x improvement, because toArray is a bulk arraycopy.

FrameDecoder.feed, reported only to close out the refuted premise, not as a win:
  512 KiB   9 chunks  0.06 ms
 1024 KiB  17 chunks  0.08 ms
 2048 KiB  33 chunks  0.03 ms
 4096 KiB  65 chunks  0.03 ms
Still flat, as it was before. The before note was right that there was no quadratic
behaviour to fix here. This path was never the problem and should not be cited as a
benefit of this bead.

BYTE IDENTITY. All 431 tests pass across 13 modules, including the committed golden
literals in AgentDomainJsonSuite, AgentSchedulerShapeSuite, StructuredResultCodecSuite
and VersionedJsonSuite, none of which were edited. scalafmtCheckAll is clean.

One real gap surfaced while proving identity and is now closed. encodeSubmitRequest
puts an inline script's bytes on the wire through circe's derived ScriptSource codec,
and no golden test covered ScriptSource.Inline: every existing golden used
ExistingRemote, which carries no bytes. The derived codec emitted a JSON array of byte
numbers when the field was a Vector[Byte], so a plain swap to ByteVector would have
silently changed that wire format with nothing to catch it. Explicit Encoder/Decoder
instances for ByteVector reproduce the numeric shape, and a new test pins the exact
literal {"Inline":{"name":"run.sh","bytes":[35,33,...]}}.

Noted for P7.4: this object now has two byte encodings on purpose, the derived numeric
array and the hand-written base64 used by encodeScriptProgram. That inconsistency
predates this bead and belongs to codec ownership, not to a representation swap.
